描述_ZN: Cai Zhi Tu" scroll, Yongzheng, Qing dynasty, ink and wash on paper, 204 cm long and 131 cm wide.　　On the upper right side of the painting, Hong Li inscribed himself: "Why do I come to be a dashing guest in Qingdu, free for the love of clouds and smoke? Peony basket full of immortal rocks, mango shoes do not step on the dusty world. The human world Penglai mirror in the sky, the haze scarf seems to be South China immortal. Who knows the real face of the year, the picture into the raw silk is accidental. Self-inscribed by Changchun Jushi." Inscriptions of "Prince Bao Bao" in white and "Changchun Jushi" in vermilion at the bottom, and "Leshan Hall" in white with an oval seal at the head. On the left side of the painting, Liang Shizheng writes a long inscription, inscribed "Inscribed by Liang Shizheng in the fourth month of summer of Yongzheng Jiayin", and inscribed with a round seal in vermilion and a square seal in white of "Shizheng". The year "Yongzheng Jiayin" is the twelfth year of Yongzheng (1734). Inscriptions of the Qianlong emperor's seals, such as "Eight symbols of the treasure of the oldest generation", "Five blessings and five generations of the hall of the oldest generation" and "The treasure of the emperor", are on the upper part of the painting.　　The picture depicts a young man in Han Chinese dress, holding a ruyi in one hand and holding a plum deer in the other, looking calmly. Beside him stands a young man with a basket and a hoe, whose eyebrows and features and melon face look similar to those of the young man, and their faces are very close to the "court dress image" of Hongli's ascension to the throne. According to the word "self-titled" in the poem inscribed by Hongli, "Changchun Jushi", it is inferred that this picture should be a portrait of Hongli when he was young and a teenager. It is also known from the inscription of "Prince Bao Bao" by Hongli that this picture should be painted between the eleventh (1733) and thirteenth years of Yongzheng, that is, between the ages of 23 and 25 when Hongli was crowned "Prince Bao" by the Yongzheng Emperor, and according to the ink inscription of Liang Shizheng in the picture "Yongzheng Jiayin", it can be further determined that this picture is a portrait of Hongli when he was 23 or 24 years old.　　The figures in the picture are modeled in white, the face is drawn in light ink, the clothes are drawn in thick ink, and the lines are in light and light, rigid and soft, accurately expressing the different physical and physiological features of the figures, which shows the author's strong skill in shaping with lines.
